text:
elaine_support: FYI - Customer ACME reported a big p95 jump (~2.5x) on API requests (auth token refresh + /v1/embeddings) starting ~03:15 UTC. Happened right after the CUDA/driver rollout in eu-west. Customers seeing 400-800ms -> 2s+ for auth calls.

samir_ops: grabbing graphs now. linking p95 heatmap and host IO metrics. looks like host io await and nvme qdepth spiked ~03:12 UTC on the same nodes serving their traffic.

infra_bot: deploy-bot: "deploy: cuda-driver-535.6 rolled out to eu-west-prod (batch 3/5) at 03:10 UTC" :information_source:

tony_sre: can anyone repro locally or on staging with the same driver? want to know if it's driver+kernel interaction or just coincidental IO noise.

mika_repro: repro steps I ran on a eu-like node:
```
# warm KV cache then hammer auth + embed calls
for i in {1..100}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
    -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"foo"}' >/dev/null &
done
```
Result: p95 ~1.8s, iostat shows /dev/nvme0n1 await jumping to 25-40ms and util ~98%.

samir_ops: matching logs - dmesg shows a few "nvme 0: completion queue timeout" messages around 03:12 on the affected hosts. not widespread, concentrated on nodes in the driver rollout batch.

tony_sre: hypothesis: new driver exposes a latent host-kernel NVMe scheduling regression under our IO pattern (small random reads for KV cache + GC). Could amplify auth latency since token validation touches the user cache.

elaine_support: customer wants ETA and mitigation. we should avoid full rollback if possible. any quick mitigations we can do to reduce customer impact?

mika_repro: quick options:
- route auth/billing traffic away from rollout batch to remaining nodes (routing fallback)
- enable read-prefetch/pinned KV cache on nodes that remain on old driver
- temporarily increase allowed qdepth on host (sysctl/driver knob) to absorb bursts
- if needed, rollback driver on the small affected pool

samir_ops: I'm starting an emergency routing rule to steer customer ACME's traffic to eu-west pool A (still on driver 534.x). will also enable a temporary token-cache TTL extension for their sessions to reduce auth calls.

tony_sre: I'll open a small canary rollback run for batch 3 (3/12 nodes) so we can see if p95 drops after reverting to 534.x. rolling rollback to 534 on those nodes and then monitor.

infra_bot: alert: routing-change applied for tenant:acme -> eu-west-pool-a, 03:30 UTC.

mika_repro: for visibility, here's a short snippet from iostat and dmesg we collected: 
```
Device            r/s     w/s    rkB/s    wkB/s  await  util
nvme0n1         120.4  220.1   4800    17000   28.4  98.1
[  +0.112345] nvme nvme0: completion queue timeout
[  +0.000456] nvme nvme0: aborting command
```

samir_ops: after routing change p95 for ACME auth dropped from ~2.1s to ~480ms within two minutes. KV misses still heavier but acceptable.

elaine_support: told the customer we applied routing fallback and extended token TTL. customer acknowledged and asked for follow-up postmortem and mitigation timeline.

tony_sre: plan next 3 hrs: 1) finish canary rollback on batch 3, 2) if rollback fixes p95, schedule rollback for remaining rolled nodes overnight (with paging and pre-announce), 3) run NVMe firmware health checks and coordinate with vendor if time permits, 4) investigate kernel scheduler tunables for NVMe qdepth.

samir_ops: also adding a temporary autoscale bump for auth endpoints to absorb bursts during mitigation. updated runbook entry: mark driver-535 rollout paused until triage complete.

mika_repro: capturing repro artifacts and saving to incident bucket: s3://incidents/8267890123/artifacts.tar.gz (contains iostat, dmesg, perf top).

elaine_support: thanks team. I'll send the customer a short status note: "we routed your traffic and extended token TTL to reduce auth load, investigating a driver/IO interaction; we'll follow up with root cause and timeline." :thumbsup:

tony_sre: quick note for postmortem: include exact kernel version matrix for affected hosts, which firmware revisions were present on NVMe, and our KV cache eviction pattern metrics.

infra_bot: monitor: p95 auth (acme): 480ms -> 520ms -> stable. closing immediate customer escalation flow. Incident owner: tony_sre.

elaine_support: closing thread here, will re-open if latency resurfaces or rollback shows no improvement. thanks all. :coffee:
